content:
maria: quick heads-up — during the viewer/editor role split rollout i found a path where project viewers still see the "Edit settings" button for template projects. repro steps below. :eyes:
ajay: can you drop the repro steps? sounds high-impact if viewers can trigger editors flows
maria: repro:
1) create new org with legacy role mapping enabled
2) invite user with role "viewer" via invite link from legacy team template
3) open project > settings > templates -> 'Edit' button is visible and UI route loads editor form
Observed: client-side gating allowed the UI to surface edit controls; server-side permission check currently blocks the backend mutate call, so no writes happened. still means confusing surface area + potential phishing vector.
sam: good catch. do we see any KMS or audit events tied to this? if backend blocked, KMS keys shouldn't be used but worth checking.
kevin: i queried crypto logs earlier for the last 24h — nothing suspicious for Decrypt/AsymmetricSign on that project key. for completeness, run this (GCP):
```
resource.type="kms_key"
protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
resource.labels.key_id="projects/myproj/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/my-key"
```
and check timestamp around the repro user.
olivia: thanks — this matches my local. the bigger issue is the inconsistent UX and legacy role mappings granting a derived `project:edit` flag in the client. we introduced a `legacy_team_default` mapping during the refactor which is too permissive.
ajay: can you paste the mapping snippet? we'll want a minimal patch plus a migration that backfills correct role bindings for older orgs.
maria: mapping snippet:
```
# legacy mapping
"team_roles": {
  "legacy_team_default": ["viewer", "editor"],
  "template_owner": ["admin"]
}
```
we inadvertently treated `legacy_team_default` as additive instead of explicit.
olivia: plan proposal:
- patch client to hide edit controls unless `has_permission('project.edit')` is returned by /v1/permissions (soft-fail to deny)
- server: tighten legacy mapping to remove implicit editor grant; add feature-flagged rollout
- migration: compute delta of memberships that would lose editor and send notification emails + 7-day grace with audit logging enabled
- canary: roll change to 3% of orgs, watch console telemetry and support tickets
ajay: agree. add a server-side assert to log mismatches between client-surface and server-check to Sentry. also add an integration test for the template UI route that asserts server denies mutation for viewers.
sam: on KMS/audit side: i'll add an aggregation to detect any unexpected key usage coming from UI flows that previously were only editor-accessible. i'd also add an alert rule: if there's a Decrypt call from a principal who has no `editor` binding in IAM for that project, fire P1 to eng-security.
kevin: for audit queries add this elastic example we use in the console: `index: audit-*, query: event.action: "UNWRAP_KEY" AND actor: user:* AND NOT role: editor` — tweak for our schema. i'll add a saved dashboard.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for service=console-auth-config, version=2.14.3-canary, target=3% orgs :rocket:
olivia: assign owners:
- maria: produce minimal rollback-safe server patch removing legacy editor grant (PR + tests)
- ajay: migration script and email template, infra test for backfill
- sam: KMS audit queries + alert rule
- kevin: dashboard + saved query + Sentry mapping
- olivia: client gating patch + rollout plan
maria: i'll open a PR this afternoon. quick question for kevin/sam: do we need a KMS key rotation or any immediate key policy change? i think not since no decrypts happened, but want sign-off.
sam: no rotation yet. recommend watch-only for 72h, then reassess. add `kms.watch` tag to the incident so on-call sees it.
kevin: agree — no rotation. we'll keep a sticky note in the audit dashboard and tag any related tickets.
ajay: script prototype: `rbac migrate-legacy --dry-run --org-list=legacy-orgs.csv > backfill-plan.json` will produce a list of users losing editor. once dry-run vetted, we'll notify and then run with `--apply`.
maria: ok going to triage, PR link coming. thanks all. :lock:
deploy-bot: canary deployment completed successfully for version=2.14.3-canary, duration=9m12s :white_check_mark:
olivia: will monitor telemetry and escalate if anything odd shows up. followups in #eng-security tomorrow 10am sync.
kevin: noted. i'll snapshot audit indices and export quick-run queries for the team.
